summary: Most quality loss comes from splitting inside tightly bound units — before a clause's final verb, inside causal/parallel chains, or right after reason connectives — which strands referents and predicates. Meanwhile many perfect-quality sentences are left whole or under-split even though sentence-initial discourse markers, fillers, or post-question-mark boundaries offer free latency gains. The prompt needs sharper rules for where NOT to cut (predicate/referent-adjacent spots) and a default nudge to cut after leading fillers/discourse markers when quality is already safe.
